newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee slides to day's lows, then recovers.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee slides to day's lows, then recovers.

text.p: CSCE coffee swung sharply lower at midday but quickly pared their losses, as speculators focused on adjusting positions ahead of May's first notice day, dealers said.
Spot May delivery zig-zagged over a huge 14.00-cent range in the first few hours of trading, as an early run to new contract highs was met with heavy speculative liquidation.
A second round of profit-taking dragged May through support at 217 and 213 cents, pushing the spot month to a low of 210 before scattered roaster buying emerged.
"The whole rally has been liquidating Mays before first notice day," one trader said. "May-July got offered at 21 cents, which put pressure on may and the rest of the market came off in sympathy."
The May contract goes into notice period on Tuesday. Some 5,044 lots open interest remained as of Friday's close, but traders estimated an additional 1,000-2,000 positions were squared away today.
At 1252 EDT, spot May was 3.05 cents lower, at 213.50 cents a lb, while most-activea July was traded at 190.75, down 3.40 cents.
Traders said an unsually low participation in the market was partly to blame for today's volatile price action.
In addition to a national holiday in top-grower Brazil, many participants were away at the Specialty Coffee Association's annual convention in New Orleans. The conference ends today.
An estimated 7,258 lots had been exchanged as of 1230 EDT.

Meanwhile, a truckers' strike continued into its second day in Colombia. Union and government officials have scheduled talks aimed at resolving the strike for later today. ((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
